title: Living and Non-living Things
seo_title: Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology: Living and Non-living Things Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology: Living and non-living things
standard_text: Living things carry out life processes (moving, feeding, breathing, growing, reproducing, excreting and sensing); non-living things do not. Plants and animals have different structures for these life processes. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 4, Life and Living: Living and non-living things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): the seven life processes, living and non-living things, and the parts of plants and animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things move, feed, breathe, grow, reproduce, excrete and sense.
key_sub: Non-living things cannot do all seven.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things carry out seven life processes: they move, feed (get food), breathe, grow, reproduce (make young), excrete (get rid of waste) and sense (respond to their surroundings). A stone, water and a car are non-living: they cannot do all seven.

Plants and animals have parts that help them stay alive. A plant has roots, a stem, leaves, flowers and seeds. Animals have body parts for moving, feeding, breathing and sensing, such as legs, wings, mouths, gills and eyes.

Example

A car moves and uses fuel. Is it living?

Can it grow or reproduce?

Answer: no, it is non-living

Example

Which life process is a seed doing when it becomes a seedling?

It gets bigger.

Answer: growing

Common mistakes

  • Thinking anything that moves is alive.
  • Thinking plants are not living because they do not walk.
  • Forgetting that dead things were once living.
